test_title: SSC CGL Tier-II (AAO) 2023 Official Paper-III (Held On: 27 Oct, 2023 Shift 2)
subject: general
question: If the proportionate change in supply is more than proportionate change in the price, it is said to be:
solution:
The correct answer is** relatively elastic supply.**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__**

__
 
• **Relatively elastic supply:**

 
 
• When the proportionate change in supply is more than the proportionate change in price, it indicates that suppliers are very responsive to price changes.
 
• This situation is termed as relatively elastic supply, meaning that a small change in price leads to a larger change in the quantity supplied.
 
• In financial enterprises, this could be observed in markets where production can be increased or decreased quickly without significant cost, such as the market for digital products or services.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Perfectly elastic supply:**

 
 
• This is incorrect. Perfectly elastic supply means that suppliers are willing to supply any amount of goods at a specific price, and any change in price will cause the supply to drop to zero or become infinite. This is an extreme and rare situation.
 
 
 
• **Relatively inelastic supply:**
 
 
• This is incorrect. Relatively inelastic supply means that the proportionate change in supply is less than the proportionate change in price. Suppliers are not very responsive to price changes in this case.
 
 
 
• **Unitary elastic supply:**
 
 
• This is incorrect. Unitary elastic supply means that the proportionate change in supply is exactly equal to the proportionate change in price. The supply responsiveness is directly proportional to price changes.
